stub_note: Elements with attributes the source leaves silent hold the attribute stub an honest run writes: generate_attribute_stubs output for the element's class, with the fields the source settles set to their key values and every other field null. The generator ran with the pinned module's class templates, which are the platform's in content. Exposures the platform computes from a null field are the platform's output on an honest null stub, not a fact about the system. Known limits: exposure truth comes from one class per element, so x-idp and x-logplatform under an allowed alternate class produce other exposure names; and the boundaries' enforcement fields (implicit_deny_enabled, allow_any_inbound, egress_filtering) are not in the Network Segment template, so their stubs do not hold them. d-admin-commands under User Input has no tls_only_transport field, so its plaintext channel shows only on f-bastion-admin, and its exposure truth is System Configuration's.

pass_through.rule: a run that draws a load balancer the source declares as its own component still has the key flow: a chain A -> X -> B counts as the key flow A -> B when the key flow is listed here, both hops run forward, X matches no key component by alias and is not a decoy, X has one of these classes (or, unclassified, a name with one of these aliases), and X carries only that bridge (every flow on X connects it to the flow's source or target). Neither hop may be a decoy, and X does not bridge when its class is a class (or class alternate) of a key component the run left unmatched. Attributes of the bridged flow: a transit key holds as insecure when either hop states plaintext, and as secure only when both hops state it; every other key (auth and credentials included) is read from the hop into the target, or from the source hop when the target hop does not state it. A data item is carried only when both hops carry it.

out_of_model.rule: Out of this model: cluster plumbing that the external-secrets operator runs. Its controller pulls from the ClusterSecretStore cloud-secrets, which the repository never defines, into Kubernetes Secrets (gateway-log-ingest in deploy/edge/gateway-deployment.yaml); the gateway reads its key from its environment and never calls the store. Secret delivery is a credential-storage attribute of the workload, not a data flow, and no source or sheet fact supplies the C3 or C8 fields of a flow to the store. A run that models the store and its flows cannot pass Gate 3 on them; the gate3-loopback reply tells it to remove them and to keep the Secret and the key the gateway reads. Not scored by the rubric (an unmatched flow scores nothing, and the store is no decoy); the first Gate 3 counts such a flow as outside gate3_ceiling. Known limit: a store named after a key component ("Gateway Secret Store") matches that component by alias.

red_flag_rule: each red flag must be present in the persisted attributes (or zoning findings) and named in the Step 9 output. Named: the eligible text mentions one of its step9_phrases, as whole words, case-insensitive, with '_', '-', '*' and backticks read as spaces and runs of whitespace as one space, on both sides. Eligible text: the assistant text from the Step 9 marker up to the push-consent prompt, and the markdown files the run wrote in that interval. Also named: every assertion of the flag has a condition that one block of the review relay (what the main session says after a reviewer run returns, up to its next question) states by the element's name or id with the condition's field and its insecure value; for a flow, naming both of its ends also names it.
red_flag_limits: Phrase matching cannot tell a finding from every other use of its words. Known limits: 'HTTP upstream' also matches 'HTTP upstream timeout'; a bare 'X-Customer-Id' matches any mention of the header; 'flat network' matches a hypothetical ('a flat network would'); 'under-segmented' can refer to something other than the data boundary; and 'under-protected' cannot tell the required b-data finding from the allowed b-edge, b-orders and b-ops ones. A 'no' before a phrase still names its flag ('no card numbers are stored in plaintext'); 'admin listener' also covers Kong's own admin_listen; 'DB credential is shared' also covers the orders_admin credential engineers share. A hyphen reads as a space, so a phrase also matches inside a compound ('SSH is open to the internet-facing bastion only from the VPN'); and a hedge still names its flag ('whether the DB credential is shared is unknown'). 'Orders Database: not TLS-only' names only the missing server-side TLS enforcement, not the orders API's plaintext connection, and matches only that label-and-condition form. 'Shared DB credential' and 'share the DB credential' also cover the orders_admin credential engineers share. 'SSH open to any address' also matches a scoped continuation ('SSH open to any address in the VPN range'). 'customer_email goes to the log platform' also matches a sentence that goes on to say the value is redacted or hashed. 'share orders-db-credentials' also matches a prohibition ('do not share orders-db-credentials'). 'admin listener has no auth' also covers Kong's admin_listen (RBAC off) and a qualified continuation ('has no auth beyond the network policy').

zoning.rule: required findings must appear at the full phase; allowed ones may (they follow how card data is linked); no boundary is ever proposed RESTRICTED

basis.external-ingress b-internet b-data: The on-call engineer reaches the orders database through the Ops bastion (f-engineer-bastion, then f-bastion-db). The bastion is a VPN Gateway (the bastion variants of the sheet's model-review-confirm and classification-confirm replies), a forwarder, in the operations subnet (Public), which is neither external nor trusted. The sheet ratifies only the vendor's channel, so the crossing stays unratified.
basis.external-ingress b-internet b-orders: The on-call engineer reaches the orders API's admin listener through the Ops bastion (f-engineer-bastion, then f-bastion-admin). The bastion is a VPN Gateway (the bastion variants of the sheet's model-review-confirm and classification-confirm replies), a forwarder, in the operations subnet (Public), which is neither external nor trusted. The sheet ratifies only the vendor's channel, so the crossing stays unratified.

c2.rule: C2 is reachable without waivers from source and sheet in every combination: the worst, bastion_missed-webhook_tier2-orders_api_tier3, is 81.1 % answerable, so a run there needs to capture 98.6 % of what it can answer. The capture rate a run needs is 80 / answerable_pct. C2 is judged at the final Gate 3, after the operator has stated the platform facts in the first gate3-loopback reply; the fields resting on them are sheet fields from that reply. The webhook receiver alone is 61.5 % answerable, and the lowest source share is 59.5 %. reachable_with_implied_pct also counts the not-applicable and silent fields whose value the key accepts

gate3_ceiling.rule: A run that follows the answer sheet cannot know some platform facts until the operator states them: that the cluster enforces the NetworkPolicies, how the log platform and the payment vendor treat a missing or invalid key, which database account the services log in as, and where their database password is kept. A bar run gives each at the Step 8 relay when a row of its tables asks for it, a loopback run in the first gate3-loopback reply; a field whose fact an operator reply gave before the first showing's gates result leaves the ceiling. Its first Gate 3 therefore fails only on the fields below whose facts are still to come, C2 aside (C2 is judged at the final Gate 3, and the account and password facts settle C2 fields only): C3 on the four log flows and the vendor flow, and C8 on the edge gateway, the orders API and the webhook receiver (C8 lists Tier 1 and 2 components only). A failure outside this set at the first showing is modelling work left unfinished. Once the facts are given, a run that follows the sheet passes Gate 3 without waivers.

quick.rule: A quick run is held to the items below. The scoped items are scored on the priority subset: the elements the Step 8 snapshot holds on this fixture (the Tier 1-2 components and flows Gate 3's C2 and C8 list before enrichment, the crown-jewel elements and the cross-boundary pivots). An assertion counts only when every element it names is in the subset, a red flag only when its assertions all do. Controls are deferred in quick mode and are not scored; Gate 3 completeness beyond the subset is not held.
